theme: Pentecost, the Spirit poured on all flesh
readingInstruction: Read Acts 2:1-47. The Spirit falls on Pentecost, Peter preaches the first Christian sermon, three thousand repent, and the new community forms. You have already studied the Spirit and repentance in doctrinal pauses. Today, read the narrative as a whole.
settingTheScene: Pentecost, fifty days after Passover, was one of three pilgrim feasts. Jerusalem was crowded with Jews from across the Roman world. The disciples were gathered together when the Spirit came. Peter’s sermon is a model of apostolic preaching: it explains the event from the Scriptures, proclaims the death and resurrection of Jesus, and calls for repentance.
observation: “When the day of Pentecost arrived, they were all together in one place” (2:1).
“We hear them telling in our own tongues the mighty works of God” (2:11).
“And it shall come to pass that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved” (2:21).
“This Jesus, delivered up according to the definite plan and foreknowledge of God, you crucified and killed by the hands of lawless men” (2:23).
“Being therefore exalted at the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this that you yourselves are seeing and hearing” (2:33).
“Let all the house of Israel therefore know for certain that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified” (2:36).
“And all who believed were together and had all things in common” (2:44).
“Praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved” (2:47).
interpretation:
The Spirit comes on the disciples as promised. The visitors from many nations are amazed to hear the apostles speaking about the mighty works of God in their own languages. Some are perplexed, and others mock. Peter stands with the eleven and explains: this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel. In the last days, God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh. The day of the LORD has begun.

Peter then preaches Christ. Jesus of Nazareth was a man attested by God with mighty works, wonders, and signs. He was delivered up by the definite plan and foreknowledge of God, and killed by lawless men. Both are true: God’s plan and human guilt. But God raised him up, because it was not possible for death to hold him. Peter cites Psalm 16: David spoke of the resurrection of the Christ. David died and his tomb is here, but David was a prophet, and he spoke of one of his descendants. Peter then cites Psalm 110: “The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand.” Jesus is exalted, and from the right hand he has poured out the Spirit. “Let all the house of Israel therefore know for certain that God has made him both Lord and Christ.”

The result is conviction. Peter calls them to repent and be baptized, and about three thousand are added. Then Luke gives a picture of the new community. They devote themselves to the apostles’ teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread, and prayer. Awe comes on every soul, and many wonders and signs are done by the apostles. They have all things in common, selling possessions to give to anyone in need. Day by day they attend the temple together and break bread in their homes with glad and generous hearts. They have favor with all the people, and the Lord adds to their number daily those who are being saved.

This is the birth of the church. It is not a human organization but a work of the Spirit, centered on the risen Christ. Its marks are Word, fellowship, sacrament, prayer, generosity, joy, and evangelism.
connection: Joel 2:28-32 is the prophecy fulfilled. Psalm 16:8-11 and Psalm 110:1 are Peter’s texts. Leviticus 23:15-22 describes the Feast of Weeks. Exodus 19 and 20 recall the giving of the law at Sinai, as Pentecost came to be associated with it. Genesis 11 is Babel. Ezekiel 36:26-27 and Jeremiah 31:33 fit the new covenant. Romans 8:9 and Ephesians 2:19-22 describe the Spirit and the church. 1 John 3:17-18 teaches generosity.
application:
Read the sermon (2:14-41) aloud. Notice how Peter uses Scripture and then calls for a response.

Which of the marks of the early church would you like to see more in your own church? Pray for it.

Share something with someone in need this week, as the first believers did.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for pouring out the Spirit on his people.
Tell him what it means that he is both Lord and Christ.
Ask him to fill you with his Spirit.
